questions.q: What is a reversible change?
questions.a: A change that can be undone, bringing back the original state - melting ice to water and freezing it back.

questions.q: Give two examples of reversible changes.
questions.a: Melting of ice and stretching of a rubber band (also folding paper).

questions.q: Why is inflating a balloon reversible but bursting it not?
questions.a: Deflating restores the balloon; a burst balloon's original state cannot return.

questions.q: What is an irreversible change?
questions.a: A change that cannot be undone to get the original material back - burning paper, cooking an egg.

questions.q: Give two examples of irreversible changes.
questions.a: Burning of paper and souring of milk (also growth of a plant).

questions.q: How is cutting of paper different from burning it?
questions.a: Cutting is a reversible physical change (pieces can be rejoined); burning makes ash - irreversible.

questions.q: What happens to a metal rod on heating?
questions.a: It expands - becomes a little longer and thicker (thermal expansion).

questions.q: Give one everyday example of expansion by heat.
questions.a: Railway gaps, or a jam jar lid loosened under hot water.

questions.q: Why are gaps left between railway tracks?
questions.a: In summer the rails expand; gaps prevent bending of the track.

questions.q: What happens to a substance on cooling?
questions.a: It contracts - becomes smaller (thermal contraction).

questions.q: Give one example of contraction on cooling.
questions.a: A metal ring tightening on a wooden wheel when cooled, or a lid tightening in the fridge.

questions.q: Do all materials contract equally on cooling?
questions.a: No - the amount differs from material to material.

questions.q: What happens when substances are mixed?
questions.a: They may simply mix (salt in water) or react forming new substances (lime in water heats up).

questions.q: Give one example of mixing that is only physical.
questions.a: Mixing sand and salt - both stay the same and can be separated.

questions.q: Give one example where mixing causes a chemical change.
questions.a: Mixing lime in water (slaking) releases heat - a new substance forms.

concepts.title: Change in Length due to Burning

questions.q: A 30 cm candle burns down to 18 cm. How much length is lost?
questions.a: 12 cm

questions.q: A 50 cm stick is burnt and only 32 cm remains. Find the length lost.
questions.a: 18 cm

questions.q: Burning reduced a 25 cm wick to 9 cm. Calculate the loss in length.
questions.a: 16 cm

questions.q: A 100 m cloth roll shrinks after washing to 98.5 m. What length is lost?
A 12 cm incense stick burns to 4 cm. How many cm burned away?
questions.a: 8 cm

solution_steps.name: weight_ratio
solution_steps.explain: current weight as a multiple of the earlier one

questions.q: A kitten weighed 800 g last month and 1050 g now. Find its weight gain.
A child's weight rose from 22 kg to 25 kg in a year. Calculate the gain.
questions.a: 3 kg

questions.q: A plant pot went from 1.2 kg to 1.65 kg as the plant grew. What is the gain?
A calf weighed 30 kg and now weighs 41 kg. How much has it gained?
questions.a: 11 kg

questions.q: A pup's weight increased from 2.4 kg to 3.1 kg. Find the weight gained.
questions.a: 0.7 kg
